item.title: Hadron 1.0.3
item.description:
• Wine 11.21, Wine Staging 11.21 and Wine 11.21 for Apple Silicon can be downloaded. Wine 11.15 stays the default.
  • Steam Settings > Compatibility has Default Compatibility Settings: pick the graphics backend and other options once, for all Rosetta or FEX tools or for one runtime. A game follows them unless it has its own settings.
  • A new Winetricks window in the Prefixes view shows what can be installed into a game's prefix, and installs it.
  • Games protected by Steam CEG now start.
  • Games start faster. Hadron skips the registry import when a prefix already has its settings, and the Prefixes view lists prefixes before it has measured their sizes.
  • If a game crashes right after you move it to another Wine runtime, the next launch offers to rebuild its prefix, with a backup if you want one. Your saves are kept.
  • AVX2 is now advertised to Rosetta by default, and FEX uses reduced x87 precision by default, which makes games faster. Each game's Hadron settings can turn either off.
  • A launch option such as HADRON_ENV_FOO=bar gives the game FOO=bar, for variables Hadron has no setting for.
  • Plug-ins in ~/Library/Application Support/hadron/plugins show up as rows in a Developer section of a game's Hadron settings.
  • Hadron is available in German and French.
  • Works with Steam client 1792618285 and beta 1792626604.
  • Tuxera NTFS is not supported, because a bug in its driver can corrupt files.
  • Closing a Ubisoft game such as Trackmania now closes Ubisoft Connect too, about 15 seconds later, so Steam sees the game has stopped. Before, Ubisoft Connect kept running and Steam showed the game as still running.
  • Steam's library filter can show only Windows games, and the Mac filter no longer lists Windows games.
  • Windows programs added to Steam as non-Steam games run with Hadron's default compatibility tool, and their prefixes are named after the shortcut.
  • Steam no longer takes the focus away from a game while it starts.
  • High Resolution also doubles Windows' text and interface scaling, so games are not drawn at half size, and turning it off halves it again.
  • The Mac keeps its display awake while a game runs.
  • Games that install Microsoft's Visual C++ runtime use it instead of Wine's copy, which fixes Unreal games that said the runtime was missing.
  • Hadron and its Steam settings are available in Italian.
  • Fixes from NotProton for Steam installed on another drive, Valve downloads that stalled, and changes to a prefix while a game used it.

item.title: Hadron 1.0.2
item.description:
• Runtime downloads show a progress bar with megabytes and a percentage, and can be stopped. Before, the download said 0% until it had finished.
  • Wine 11.19 for Apple Silicon can be downloaded. It runs x86 games with FEX instead of Rosetta and needs macOS 26.5.
  • The Update and Repair rows say which Hadron is installed for Steam and which this app brings.
  • A new build of Hadron no longer shows as an update when only the signatures of its helper programs changed.
  • A supported runtime that is not on this Mac and cannot be downloaded yet keeps a row that says so, instead of vanishing from the list.

item.title: Hadron 1.0.1
item.description:
The first release with automatic updates.

  • Updates: Hadron is signed with Developer ID, notarized by Apple, and updates itself through Sparkle. Hadron → Check for Updates… works.
  • Runtime downloads: Wine 11.15, Wine Staging 11.15, Wine 11.19 and CrossOver Wine 26.3 can be downloaded from the Status page, checked and set up in one step. CrossOver's download comes without D3DMetal; Add D3DMetal… takes it from Apple's Game Porting Toolkit or CrossOver on your Mac.
  • Launch window: while a game starts, a small window shows each step, the game's Windows processes, both logs, and a warning when nothing happens for 30 seconds, with Stop Game and Save Diagnostics. The Launches section keeps recent launches.
  • Controllers: Steam Input's virtual pad reaches games, with its buttons in the right order. Before, games under every runtime saw no controller.
  • Steam's permissions: Steam keeps its input and device permissions across Hadron updates, because Hadron signs it with a stable identity of its own instead of ad hoc.
  • Switching runtimes: a game's prefix moves between the Rosetta and Apple Silicon runtimes in place, instead of asking for a rebuild. Moving back to CrossOver works too.
  • Apple Silicon: Ubisoft Connect, and with it Trackmania, starts under FEX.
  • Open Steam in the toolbar and the Setup menu, a new icon, and the Status page follows Steam quitting and starting.
